description: Create an Airflow watchdog DAG for logistics_co that detects long-running and stuck DAG runs across the deployment. Every 10 minutes it should: (1) query the Airflow metadata database (via the REST API or a read-only session) for DAG runs in state 'running' or 'queued', (2) compare each run's elapsed time against a baseline of the p95 duration of that DAG's last 30 successful runs, alerting when elapsed > max(2 x p95, 15 minutes), (3) detect task instances stuck in 'queued' for more than 20 minutes, (4) send alerts grouped by owner, (5) exclude DAGs tagged 'no-watchdog' and the watchdog itself.

schema.target: Slack channels mapped from DAG owner

edge_cases: DAGs with fewer than 5 successful runs have no reliable baseline and must use a fixed default threshold
Elapsed time must use start_date of the run, not logical_date; backfill runs have old logical dates but recent start dates
Baseline must include only successful scheduled runs, excluding manual and backfill run types
Sensor-heavy DAGs in reschedule mode legitimately run for hours; thresholds must come from their own baseline
The watchdog must be read-only and must not clear or mark tasks
common_failure_modes: FM2: Elapsed computed from logical_date flags every backfill run as stuck
FM3: Baseline averaged over all runs, including failed ones that ended early, underestimates normal duration
FM6: Watchdog monitoring itself creates self-referential alerts when the scheduler is slow
